**VERDICT: REVISE** **Overall Assessment**: The `DataLoader` component implements visual loading feedback but completely fails to communicate asynchronous state transitions to assistive technology. While automated linters and basic compliance scanners will pass this component because there are no invalid attributes or inaccessible form elements, real screen reader users are left in indefinite silence when data arrives, and users with vestibular disorders are subjected to unconstrained infinite CSS animation. --- ### Pre-commitment Predictions Prior to detailed inspection of this async data-loading pattern, the predicted accessibility design gaps were: 1. **Missing live region / status announcements**: Swapping loading DOM for results DOM without `role="status"` or `aria-live="polite"`. 2. **Missing `aria-busy`**: Container fails to signal an ongoing mutation to the accessibility tree. 3. **Motion sensitivity omission**: Continuous CSS spinner animation lacking `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`. 4. **Unhandled error state**: Happy-path-only async logic lacking failure communication (`role="alert"`). *Post-investigation outcome*: All 4 predictions were confirmed in the implementation. --- ### Critical Findings (blocks access) *None.* *(Note: Complete silence during async updates was evaluated under Phase 8 Realist Check for CRITICAL severity. Because the loaded data remains accessible if the user manually re-navigates the DOM with a virtual cursor, it does not completely trap or block access, so it is calibrated to MAJOR rather than CRITICAL).* --- ### Major Findings (significantly degrades experience) #### 1. Asynchronous content replacement is completely unannounced to assistive technology - **Confidence**: HIGH - **File & Lines**: [`DataLoader.jsx:14-27`](file:///DataLoader.jsx#L14-L27) - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS). - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages (Level AA); WAI-ARIA 1.2 Status pattern. - **Why this matters**: When `isLoading` transitions from `true` to `false`, `
` is removed and `
` is inserted into the DOM. Because neither element nor their parent `
` is a persistent live region, screen readers announce nothing. A non-sighted user hearing "Loading data..." will wait indefinitely, unable to tell whether the request is still pending, has timed out, or has finished. - **Fix**: Provide a persistent live region or apply `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"` to the container. Note that conditionally mounting an `aria-live` container at the same time its content appears causes many screen readers to drop the announcement; the live region container must be persistent in the DOM. ``` ### A11y Evidence Finding finding_id: dynamic-content-silent-swap fingerprint: c4b89f21d30a8e1b source: DataLoader.jsx:14-27 wcag_or_apg: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages (Level AA) section_508_fpc_context: not in scope (WCAG 2.2 AA target) severity: MAJOR perspective_alarms: screen_reader=HIGH, cognitive=MEDIUM evidence: DataLoader.jsx:15,22 — conditional render inside unannounced div.data-container reproduction_steps: 1. Mount DataLoader with screen reader (VoiceOver/NVDA) active. 2. Hear "Loading data...". 3. Wait 2000ms until state updates. 4. Screen reader produces zero speech or braille output when "Results" renders. expected_behavior: Screen reader announces that content has loaded or announces the updated result title. actual_behavior: Screen reader remains silent upon data completion. trend: new ``` #### 2. Absence of `aria-busy` during active async data fetch - **Confidence**: HIGH - **File & Lines**: [`DataLoader.jsx:14`](file:///DataLoader.jsx#L14) - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users navigating while data is fetching. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A); WAI-ARIA 1.2 `aria-busy` state. - **Why this matters**: Assistive technology has no programmatic mechanism to know that `.data-container` is in a transitional, incomplete state. Without `aria-busy="true"`, screen readers may attempt to parse or present the container's contents as finished content rather than an active transaction. - **Fix**: Add `aria-busy={isLoading}` to the container element: ```jsx
``` ``` ### A11y Evidence Finding finding_id: missing-aria-busy-state fingerprint: a77e31f902dc65bc source: DataLoader.jsx:14 wcag_or_apg: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A) section_508_fpc_context: not in scope severity: MAJOR perspective_alarms: screen_reader=HIGH evidence: DataLoader.jsx:14
lacks aria-busy attribute reproduction_steps: Inspect DOM tree and accessibility node properties during isLoading=true. expected_behavior: Accessibility tree marks container as busy=true until loading concludes. actual_behavior: Container has no busy state exposed. trend: new ``` #### 3. Continuous looping animation without `prefers-reduced-motion` override - **Confidence**: HIGH - **File & Lines**: [`DataLoader.css:22, 25-28`](file:///DataLoader.css#L22-L28) - **User Group Impacted**: Users with vestibular disorders, motion sensitivity, and inner-ear balance conditions. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (Level A); WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (Level AAA). - **Why this matters**: `.spinner` executes an infinite rotation (`animation: spin 1s linear infinite`). For users with vestibular sensitivity, looping rotary motion can induce dizziness, nausea, and vertigo. While this fixture mocks a 2-second delay, real-world network latency or stalled requests can leave the spinner rotating indefinitely with no user control or media query suppression. - **Fix**: Introduce a `prefers-reduced-motion` media query in CSS to disable rotation or substitute a static indicator: ```css @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .spinner { animation: none; border-top-color: #0066cc; opacity: 0.8; } } ``` ``` ### A11y Evidence Finding finding_id: unconstrained-spinner-animation fingerprint: f82d914e6b12a87a source: DataLoader.css:22-28 wcag_or_apg: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (Level A) section_508_fpc_context: not in scope severity: MAJOR perspective_alarms: vestibular_and_motion=HIGH evidence: DataLoader.css:22 — animation: spin 1s linear infinite without reduced-motion query reproduction_steps: Enable "Reduce Motion" in system settings; observe spinner still executes 360-degree rotation. expected_behavior: Animation pauses, stops, or transitions to a static visual state. actual_behavior: Spinner rotates indefinitely at 1 second per cycle. trend: new ``` --- ### Minor Findings (friction but workaround exists) 1. **Decorative spinner element exposed to the accessibility tree** - **File & Lines**: [`DataLoader.jsx:17`](file:///DataLoader.jsx#L17) - **User Group**: Screen reader and Braille display users. - **WCAG Citation**: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A). - **Why this matters**: `

`. While an empty div is often ignored, it can generate extraneous blank nodes or artifacts in some assistive technology trees. - **Fix**: Add `aria-hidden="true"` to explicitly prune it from the accessibility tree: ```jsx
``` 2. **Low boundary contrast on spinner track and content borders** - **File & Lines**: [`DataLoader.css:12, 19, 32`](file:///DataLoader.css#L12-L32) - **User Group**: Low vision users and users in high-glare environments. - **WCAG Citation**: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (Level AA). - **Why this matters**: The spinner track `#f3f3f3` against white (`#ffffff`) has a contrast ratio of only **1.09:1**, and the container borders `#ddd` measure **1.36:1**, falling well below the 3:1 threshold required for graphical objects and UI boundaries. Sighted low vision users see only a floating blue arc rather than a complete track. - **Fix**: Increase border boundary contrast to at least 3:1 (e.g., `#949494` against white). --- ### Enhancements (best practice not met) 1. **Heading structure lacks landmark context** - **File & Lines**: [`DataLoader.jsx:14, 24`](file:///DataLoader.jsx#L14-L24) - **Why this matters**: The component renders `

Results

` inside a generic `div`. If embedded in a page without landmark encapsulation, screen reader users jumping by heading will encounter "Results" without clear section context. - **Fix**: Use semantic HTML `
` instead of a generic `
`. --- ### What's Missing (gaps and unhandled states) - **Missing Error Handling & Alert Communication**: The component models only the happy path. If the async call fails or times out, the component has no error state, leaving the user either stuck on the loading spinner or with empty UI. Any failure state must be accompanied by an assertive live region (`role="alert"`). - **Missing Persistent Live Region Architecture**: Dynamically inserting and removing nodes without a persistent status container prevents reliable AT announcements across browsers. - **Missing Loading Completion Confirmation**: No programmatic message confirms completion; screen reader users must manually seek out the results. --- ### Multi-Perspective Notes - **Screen reader user (NVDA, VoiceOver, JAWS)**: Upon page entry, the user hears "Loading data...". Two seconds later, visual results appear, but AT remains completely silent. The user is left hanging, unaware the process finished. - **Keyboard-only user**: No active tab stops or focus traps exist (pure data presentation). However, because focus is not moved and no live region fires, keyboard users navigating linearly must manually tab through or re-read to find new content. - **Low vision user**: The rotating `#0066cc` border segment has adequate text-grade contrast against white (4.5:1), but the background track (`#f3f3f3`) is virtually invisible (1.09:1). - **Cognitive accessibility**: Clear visual message ("Loading data..."), but if an unhandled network error occurs, cognitive load spikes due to indefinite spinning without a timeout message or recovery action. - **Vestibular & motion sensitivity**: Infinite rotary animation with no reduced-motion fallback violates user preference settings and poses a vestibular trigger. - **Auditory access**: No audio cues or media tracks involved (LOW alarm). - **Environmental contrast**: Text contrast is compliant, but boundary contrast on the card and spinner track washes out in high-ambient-light environments. --- ### Perspective Alarm Levels | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |:---|:---:|:---| | **Screen reader** | **HIGH** | Asynchronous DOM insertion without live region or status announcement | | **Keyboard-only** | **LOW** | Read-only presentation component with no interactive controls | | **Low vision** | **MEDIUM** | Low boundary contrast (`#f3f3f3` track at 1.09:1, `#ddd` border at 1.36:1) | | **Cognitive** | **MEDIUM** | No timeout or error fallback if async resolution stalls | | **Vestibular & motion** | **HIGH** | Infinite `@keyframes spin` with zero `prefers-reduced-motion` accommodation | | **Auditory access** | **LOW** | No auditory media or sound-based alerts | | **Environmental contrast** | **MEDIUM** | Sub-3:1 graphical boundaries vulnerable to washout | --- ### Recommended Remediation #### Component Code (`DataLoader.jsx`) ```jsx import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react'; While the implementation visually satisfies the requirements, it fails on two major accessibility criteria: **WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages)** by omitting live region announcements on async data delivery, and **WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide)** by failing to support `prefers-reduced-motion` on continuous rotary animation. Addressing these issues with a persistent live region and a CSS media query will elevate the component to **ACCEPT**. --- ### Open Questions (unscored) 1. **Focus intent upon completion**: In a full page workflow, will this component be preceded by an interactive search/fetch trigger?
